001: Have you started preparing for next week's presentation?
Not yet, I haven't even decided on a topic.
Didn't the teacher say you could pick a topic you're interested in?
Right, but I'm interested in too many things, so I can't figure out which one to choose.
Then just go with the field you know best.
You're right, let me think about it and I'll let you know.
002: Have you finished writing your speech?
I have a rough draft, but it feels too messy.
Why not make an outline first to sort out the main points?
I tried that, but the logic still doesn't flow well.
I can take a look and give you some suggestions.
That would be great, let's discuss it this afternoon.
003: How are you planning to open your presentation?
I want to tell a story, but I'm not sure if it's appropriate.
Telling a story is great, it can grab the audience's attention right away.
Really? I'm afraid if the story is too long, people will get impatient.
As long as you keep it under thirty seconds, it'll be fine.
Got it, I'll trim the story down a bit more.
004: How's your slide deck coming along?
I just finished it, but the pages feel a bit plain.
You could add some pictures or charts.
That makes sense, but I'm not very good at finding suitable images.
I'll recommend a few free image websites for you.
Great, thanks for helping me solve this problem.
005: How do you plan to practice your presentation?
I'm going to practice a few times in front of the mirror in my dorm.
Practicing in front of a mirror isn't enough, you should really have someone listen.
You're right, but I feel awkward asking people for help.
No problem, I can be your audience.
006: Are you planning to read from your script during the presentation?
I want to speak without it as much as possible, but I'm afraid of forgetting what to say.
You could prepare a few cue cards with just keywords on them.
That's a good idea, it's much more natural than holding the whole script.
Right, and your eye contact will be better too.
Okay, I'll go prepare the cue cards right away.
007: How many minutes are you aiming for in your presentation?
The teacher said ten minutes max, but I'm afraid I won't have enough to say.
Ten minutes is actually quite long, just give a few more examples.
That's true, the two examples I have might not be enough.
Prepare one or two more, and the time should work out.
Okay, I'll add some more specific content.
008: How do you usually calm down when you're nervous?
I usually take deep breaths and then drink some water.
I've also heard that arriving early to check out the venue helps.
Right, once you're familiar with the place, you feel much more at ease.
Then let's go look at the classroom together before the presentation.
Sure, we can head over together then.
009: How are you planning to end your presentation?
I'm going to summarize the main points and then say thank you.
That's good, but you could add one more inspiring line.
Like what? Can you give me an example?
Like, "I hope everyone will be brave enough to try new things in the future."
That's nice, I'll add that to the ending.
010: Do you need to answer questions after the presentation?
The teacher said there might be a Q&A session.
Then you'd better think ahead about what questions might be asked.
I've prepared some, but I don't know if it's enough.
If you go over the content a few more times, you should be able to handle it.
Okay, I'll practice a few more times and try to do my best.
